    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "")

### CodeQL / Incomplete multi-character sanitization

This string may still contain [<script](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/1), which may cause an HTML element injection vulnerability.

content.name: replace_string_in_file

content.text: Fixed. The single-pass `<[^>]+>` replace is what CodeQL flags — a nested/overlapping construction like `<<script>` can leave a live `<script>` tag after just one pass, since JS `replace(/…/g, …)` matches non-overlapping occurrences in one left-to-right scan rather than re-scanning the result. `stripHtml` now loops the tag-stripping regex until a pass removes nothing, so no residual tag can survive.
No errors. Since output also passes through `escapeXml` before being embedded in the SVG, this closes the CodeQL finding with defense in depth on both the sanitizer and the sink.
